A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DFIRE-based statistical energy function is a promising energy function for protein structure prediction.
a statistical energy function, which lacks a van der Waals interaction and is applied to a given structure without energy minimization, can still be used to fold helical proteins in dihedral spaces.
a dihedral-based energy minimization can be used to fold small and medium-sized proteins and to obtain near-native structures with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DFIRE-based statistical energy function, when combined with a simple repulsion energy and improper torsion energy, can be used for structure prediction by energy minimization in a dihederal space with fixed helical regions.
a simple energy function can be used to fold proteins by energy minimization in dihedral angle space with a fixed secondary structure.
a simple statistical energy function with a fixed secondary structure can produce a good decoy set with reasonable accuracy.
